## Part 1: One-Paste Command to Start / Restart the Project Anytime
Whenever you open your Codespace after it has been stopped or paused, paste this block into the Terminal to start everything fresh:

```bash
cd /workspaces/house-price-predictor

# Ensure Podman is installed (if you ever open a brand-new Codespace)
which podman >/dev/null || (sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y podman fuse-overlayfs slirp4netns)

# Create .env if missing
[ -f .env ] || cp .env.example .env

# Remove old stopped containers (keeps your volume data safe)
podman rm -f house-price-app house-price-db 2>/dev/null || true

# Create custom network and persistent volume
podman network create house-price-net 2>/dev/null || true
podman volume create house-price-pgdata 2>/dev/null || true

# Start PostgreSQL database container
podman run -d --replace \
  --name house-price-db \
  --network house-price-net \
  --network-alias db \
  --volume house-price-pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data \
  --env POSTGRES_DB=houseprices \
  --env POSTGRES_USER=houseapp \
  --env POSTGRES_PASSWORD=change-me \
  docker.io/library/postgres:16-alpine

sleep 5

# Build the web app image & start the web app container
podman build --format docker -t house-price-predictor:v1 -f Containerfile .

podman run -d --replace \
  --name house-price-app \
  --network house-price-net \
  -p 5000:5000 \
  --env DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://houseapp:change-me@db:5432/houseprices \
  --env SECRET_KEY=codespaces-secret-key \
  house-price-predictor:v1

sleep 3
podman ps
curl http://localhost:5000/health
```
*(Then in the **Ports** tab, make sure port **`5000`** is added and open in your browser.)*

## Part 2: Commands to Run in Front of Your Teacher (Presentation Flow)

### 1. Show Automated Tests & ML Model Training
*What to say:* "First, our ML pipeline cleans 12,330 Bengaluru property records, trains a scikit-learn Linear Regression model, and passes 8 automated pytest unit tests."
```bash
python -m ml.train_model
pytest
```

### 2. Show Containerfile & Built Images
*What to say:* "Here is our `Containerfile` using `python:3.12-slim`, running as a non-root user `appuser` for container security, and serving Flask via `gunicorn`. Here are our built container images."
```bash
cat Containerfile
podman images
```

### 3. Show Running Containers & Health Endpoint
*What to say:* "We have two containers running: `house-price-db` (PostgreSQL 16) and `house-price-app` (Flask/Gunicorn). Only port `5000` of the web app is exposed to the host; the database port is kept internal."
```bash
podman ps -a
curl http://localhost:5000/health
```

### 4. Show Custom Container Network (`house-price-net`)
*What to say:* "Both containers communicate over a custom bridge network `house-price-net`, allowing the web app to resolve the database container by its DNS alias `db`."
```bash
podman network ls
podman network inspect house-price-net
```

### 5. Show Persistent Volume (`house-price-pgdata`) & Container Logs
*What to say:* "Predictions are stored in PostgreSQL backed by a named Podman volume `house-price-pgdata`. Here are the live logs from both containers."
```bash
podman volume ls
podman volume inspect house-price-pgdata
podman logs house-price-app
podman logs house-price-db | tail -n 15
```

### 6. Live Demo of Volume Persistence (Teacher Favorite!)
*What to do:*
1. In the browser (port `5000`), go to **Predict**, enter **`1500`** sq ft, **`3`** BHK, **`Indiranagar`**, and click **Predict**.
2. Go to **History** and show the saved prediction.
3. Run these commands in the terminal to **destroy** and **recreate** the database container:
```bash
# Force-delete the database container
podman rm -f house-price-db
podman ps

# Recreate the database container using the SAME volume (house-price-pgdata)
podman run -d --replace \
  --name house-price-db \
  --network house-price-net \
  --network-alias db \
  --volume house-price-pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data \
  --env POSTGRES_DB=houseprices \
  --env POSTGRES_USER=houseapp \
  --env POSTGRES_PASSWORD=change-me \
  docker.io/library/postgres:16-alpine

sleep 5
podman ps
```
4. Refresh the **History** page in your browser—your prediction is **still there**, proving that the named volume persists data even when the container is destroyed!
